“After two years of running an anonymous file sharing site, we are tired of dealing with the sheer volume of users abusing it and the headache it has created for us.

We have automatically blocked the contents of hundreds of thousands of files. Forbidden filenames fell under the block, and certain usage patterns were also prohibited. As a result, the number of violations reached such an extent that we did not care if we accidentally deleted thousands of files due to a false positive of the moderation system.

Even after all this, a large amount of abuse has not stopped. This is not the job we imagined , ” said the Anonfiles team .

On each die, only one side is green and the rest are red. If you roll the green side, you win a million dollars.

Almost everyone picks the 20 sided die because their odds of winning are five percent versus only a half a percent on the 200 sided die.

The 200 sided one.

The UK has just implemented the most significant criminal justice reforms in over a decade through the Sentencing Act 2026. This legislation, which received Royal Assent in January, officially began its first phase of rollout on March 22, 2026.  
The changes are a direct response to the "gridlock" in the prison system, aiming to reduce overcrowding while introducing stricter community-based punishments.  
1. New Limits on Immediate Jail Time
As of March 22, 2026, the threshold for sending people to prison has changed:
The 12-Month Presumption: Courts are now legally required to suspend custodial sentences of 12 months or less. Judges must now grant a suspended sentence unless there are "exceptional circumstances" (e.g., specific public safety risks or domestic abuse cases).  
Expanded Suspended Sentences: Judges can now suspend sentences for up to 3 years (increased from the previous 2-year limit). This allows more offenders to be managed in the community for longer periods instead of being sent to an immediate, short-term jail cell.  
2. The "Earned Progression" Release Model
A major shift in how time is served is being phased in, with a full rollout expected by Autumn 2026:  
Release at One-Third: For Standard Determinate Sentences (SDS), the minimum point for release eligibility is dropping to 33% (one-third) of the sentence, down from the previous 40% or 50%.  
End of "Automatic" Release: Release is no longer guaranteed at the halfway point. Under the new model, prisoners must "earn" their progression through good behavior and rehabilitation. Bad behavior can now result in an Independent Adjudicator doubling additional days (from 42 up to 84 days) per incident.  
Exclusions: These early release changes do not apply to life sentences, serious violent/sexual offences, or Extended Determinate Sentences (EDS).  
3. Tougher Community "Restriction Zones"
To balance the reduction in jail time, the Act introduces high-tech community punishments:
New Prohibitions: Judges can now ban offenders from specific public events (concerts, sports), drinking establishments (pubs/clubs), or specific geographic "restriction zones."  
Massive Tagging Expansion: These bans will be enforced through a major increase in electronic monitoring and GPS tagging.  
Fixed-Term Recall (FTR): If an offender is recalled to prison for breaching their licence, the standard recall period has increased to 56 days (up from 14 or 28 days) as of March 31, 2026.
4. Why now?
The government’s annual capacity statement in early 2026 showed that without these reforms, UK prisons would have fully run out of space by June 2026. These measures aim to free up approximately 7,500 prison places by moving non-violent offenders into strict community supervision.

Apps from unverified developers will be blocked or come with big warnings and extra steps.

Google doing this to fight malware, the company says sideloaded apps are about 50 times more likely to contain bad software than Play Store apps.
